findings.title: Unsubscribe fails when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil for a user who has never visited or changed notification settings for this topic, but the action immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level`. In that common case, following the email link raises an exception instead of unsubscribing. Handle the missing row by creating it with the muted notification level (or use the existing TopicUser change helper).

findings.title: The unsubscribe action can leave the user subscribed
findings.body: When the current level is tracking or watching, this branch changes it only to regular; regular users still receive topic notifications. Since the page and email link promise to stop notifications, following the unsubscribe link must leave the user muted regardless of their starting level.

findings.title: A GET request mutates notification settings
findings.body: This action changes the user's notification level as part of a GET request. Email security scanners and link-preview bots commonly follow links automatically, so merely receiving or scanning an email can unsubscribe the recipient. Render a confirmation page on GET and perform the state change only after an explicit non-GET confirmation.
